To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Probabilistic Fasttext is a new model for multi-sense word embeddings that can also capture subword structure and uncertainty information, that it outperforms both Fasttext, which has no probability model, and dictionarylevel probabilistic embeddings, and that ProbabilisticFastText achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks that test ability to discern different word meanings.
Probabilistic Fast-Text is the first probabilistic model that can capture multi-word senses, subword structure, and uncertainty.

Probabilistic Fasttext is the first multi-sense embedding model that achieves state of the art performance on rare word benchmarks and that it is the first to capture uncertainty in its word representations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two main problems in natural language processing: 1) how to learn accurate word embeddings from small amounts of data, and 2) how to capture multiple senses of a word.
the problem of learning a probabilistic model for word embeddings, which allows for multiple senses, sub-word information, and uncertainty.
the following questions: (1) Can we develop a probabilistic model for word embeddings?

our model is the first one that is able to capture multi-sense word embeddings and at the same time to have enriched semantics on rare and unseen words.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a new probabilistic model, called Probabilistic Fast Text (PFT), for word embeddings.

we have developed a probabilistic word embedding model which has the ability to represent words in a multi-sense way while also having the ability to represent rare words and unseen words in a better manner than the existing word embedding models.
Probabilistic Fasttext is able to capture multiple word senses and sub-word structure in the form of a probabilistic model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
probabilistic models can capture uncertainty in the data, and that uncertainty can be useful in downstream tasks, such as word-similarity.
probabilistic word embeddings can be improved significantly by incorporating sub-word structures, which can be done in a principled way.
